full_judgment: 19. Mr. Ahmed Sobhan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 3 has contendent that the preparation of Form No. 'O' by the Presiding Officer is, on the face of it, full of errors. The learned Advocate has pointed out that the Presiding Officer has counted, doubly the two items of unused Ballot papers' with the result that the number of unused ballot papers has been inflated by an addition of 143. The number of the unused ballot papers was really 1776 while the Presiding Officer has shown it to be 1919. If the figure of the unused ballot papers is taken to be 1776, as found out from the correct emulation, the total number of valid papers which may be expected to be found in the ballot boxes would be 2524, Mr. Sobhan has, therefore, contended that as admittedly the total number of ballot papers which were supplied to the polling station was 4300 and the aforesaid figure for the unused ballot papers (i.e. 1776) is taken to be correct, it is found that the total number of ballot papers found in the ballot boxes namely, 2511, were not in excess at all but was rather less than the ballot papers which were issued, namely, 2524.
